entries.independent_argument: For fixed endpoint r<a, the maximum functional is continuous in the uniform path norm. Endpoint shifts have sup norm at most |r-r_next|, so crossing indicators converge off {max=a}. If max=a, since terminal r<a, attainment is before h and is captured by a countable union of events max_[0,t_k]=a. Restriction absolute continuity transfers the Brownian maximum atomlessness from reflection and the Gaussian density. Crossing events are measurable for continuous paths. The constant one has integral one on the probability space. DCT therefore yields sequential, hence ordinary, endpoint continuity; the a.e. reflection-density formula extends to every endpoint by continuity. x=c or y=c remains an immediate certain event.

At most 3R component Poisson draws plus O(R) evaluations/additions/updates per half interval produce the two marginals; each pair freezes coarse propensities across its two halves. Thus work <=C TR/h_ell for fixed finite network and T. Zero means may be assigned zero and do not increase work. Level zero uses R draws in one path step. The finite-state weak supplier gives alpha=1 under CC/DC; the coupled variance supplier gives beta=1, with base variance bounded by ||g||_infinity^2 and absorbed at h_0=T. The generic beta=1 theorem then supplies deterministic positive sample counts and work O(epsilon^-2 log(epsilon^-1)^2). Invalid-state conventions, bounded-payoff hypotheses and exclusion of guarded binomial guarantees are preserved.
